elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires Vendor to “defend” Customer from and against any covered third-party claim.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Vendor must “indemnify and hold harmless” Customer for resulting damages, losses, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates must be beneficiaries of Vendor's defence and indemnification obligations.
elements.evidence: Vendor's obligations expressly run to “Customer and its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The opening language expressly covers “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) states the required IP trigger, but the following paragraph removes coverage for certain claims involving Customer modifications, combinations, and Customer specifications. The preferred position does not authorize those exclusions.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) covers claims arising out of “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, which supplies an operative Vendor-causation requirement.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly includes Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly includes Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must provide prompt written notice, and delay excuses performance only to the extent of material prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must allow the indemnifying party to control the defence with counsel of its choice, subject to settlement protections.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from content provided by Customer for use in the Services.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The Customer indemnity expressly covers Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must not extend beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The clause additionally covers claims arising from Customer-provided “materials,” a potentially broader category than Customer-provided content.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party IP infringement or misappropriation claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) covers third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims arising from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes combinations with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided absent the combination.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims arising from Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

elements.element: The infringement remedies must include procuring the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: Vendor must, at its expense, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The infringement remedies must include modifying the affected item to be non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Vendor may be required, at Customer's option, to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing, functionally equivalent, and compliant with the Agreement.

elements.element: The infringement remedies must include replacing the affected item with a non-infringing replacement.
elements.evidence: Vendor may be required, at Customer's option, to replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item meeting the Agreement's requirements.

elements.element: The infringement remedies must include a refund if procurement, modification, or replacement is not reasonably available.
elements.evidence: If the preceding remedies are not reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive refunds of prepaid Fees for the terminated period and Fees paid for affected Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No operative provision imposes a 3× annual-fees cap. Section 21.3 merely classifies indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims and does not state the required super-cap.

result.reason: The redline supplies the principal Vendor indemnity triggers, beneficiaries, procedures, customary IP exclusions, and infringement remedies. It does not fully meet the preferred position because the IP coverage is expressly qualified by exclusions not stated in the preferred position and the Customer indemnity extends to Customer-provided “materials,” not solely content and breach of law. It does not meet fallback because no 3× annual-fees super-cap appears. The additions are coherent with the existing termination, disclaimer, and Excluded Claims provisions, although the rendered text should expressly number Sections 20.1–20.5 to make its internal cross-references unambiguous.
